machine: M1 Pro (aarch64 macOS), 10 cores, shared with other build jobs
reproduce: cargo run --release -p axil-decide --example u1_bench -- --threads N --out FILE.json; cargo test --release -p axil-decide --test u1_parity -- --ignored

parity.note: Rust and Python onnxruntime 1.22.0 produce the same float32 logits; the residual is float64 rounding in the calibration.

batched_fp32_check.model: onnx/model.onnx (fp32) of the same revision, batch-invariant
batched_fp32_check.note: The int8 model is not batch-invariant (one activation scale per batch tensor), so the runtime scores it one pair per call: padded batches of 8 move its logits by up to 1.4 and flip 4 of 249 verdicts (batch_check in benchmarks/results/typed-decisions-u1-calibration-2026-10-04.json).

latency.what: one pair per call (tokenize + run + calibrate), 249 U1 pairs; Rust after 5 warm-up pairs, Python without; one run each, Rust first
latency.load_what: Rust load = sha256 check of the pinned files + session + tokenizer, first in process (the hash check, timed alone just before with the files in the page cache, is of_which_verify_ms); Python load = session creation only
latency.caveat: One run each, on a machine still shared with other jobs (it was idle-ish, not idle). The bake-off measured Python p50 19.3 ms (onnxruntime 1.30, 4 threads) on 2026-09-27 (typed-decisions-bakeoff-2026-09-27.json). Re-measure on an idle machine and on x86 Linux before choosing where the model runs.

session_settings: Level3 is pinned: the basic level moves the int8 logits by up to 0.95 and flips 4 of 249 verdicts, while 1 to 8 threads give identical logits (session_settings_check in benchmarks/results/typed-decisions-u1-calibration-2026-10-04.json).
